death_window.end: 2020-08-04 ~16:56 (pronounced dead "about half an hour later" at hospital)
death_window.quote: At approximately 4:26 p.m., two vehicles pulled up near the 100 block of East Oak Street. Four gunmen got out, two from each vehicle, and opened fire. Weekly was shot multiple times. Two other people were wounded, a woman who was with Weekly and a man nearby. Weekly was taken to Northwestern Memorial Hospital, where he was pronounced dead about half an hour later.

medical_facts.fact: Decedent is identified in news reporting as Carlton Weekly (known as FBG Duck), age 26.
medical_facts.quote: The rapper, whose real name was Carlton Weekly, was 26.

medical_facts.fact: Weekly sustained multiple gunshot wounds; no wound locations, trajectories, calibers, or autopsy findings are present in the file.
Weekly was transported to Northwestern Memorial Hospital and pronounced dead approximately half an hour after the ~4:26 p.m. shooting on Tuesday, August 4, 2020.
medical_facts.quote: Weekly was taken to Northwestern Memorial Hospital, where he was pronounced dead about half an hour later.

medical_facts.fact: Two additional individuals—a woman with Weekly and a nearby man—were reported wounded in the same shooting, with no injury details provided.
medical_facts.quote: Two other people were wounded, a woman who was with Weekly and a man nearby.

claims.claim: FBG Duck was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon on East Oak Street in the Gold Coast.
claims.quote: Chicago rapper FBG Duck was shot and killed Tuesday afternoon on East Oak Street in the Gold Coast, one of the city's most upscale shopping districts, police said.

claims.claim: The shooting of Carlton Weekly was targeted.
claims.quote: Police said the shooting was targeted.

claims.claim: Detectives were reviewing surveillance video from the block.
claims.quote: Detectives said they were reviewing surveillance video from the block, which is lined with luxury stores and cameras.

claims.claim: Carlton Weekly was involved in an ongoing gang conflict.
claims.quote: Police said he was involved in an ongoing gang conflict.

claims.claim: Shoppers were standing on the sidewalk when two vehicles pulled up and two gunmen stepped out of each to open fire.
claims.quote: Deputy Chief O'Shea said the shoppers were standing on the sidewalk when a pair of vehicles pulled up, with two gunmen stepping out of each to open fire.

claims.claim: The shooting was a targeted attack rather than random.
claims.quote: He said the shooting was a targeted attack, not a random one.

claims.claim: Carlton Weekly had been involved in an ongoing conflict with another gang.
claims.quote: O'Shea said Weekly had been involved in an ongoing conflict with another gang.

claims.claim: Carlton Weekly had been broadcasting his travels on social media that day and was found.
claims.quote: Officers noted that Weekly had been broadcasting his travels on social media that day, and that he was found.

claims.claim: Diss tracks between FBG Duck and O Block artists fueled street violence.
claims.quote: Federal investigators later said the diss tracks between Duck and O Block artists fueled violence on the streets.

claims.claim: A bounty of $50,000, later raised to $100,000, had been offered for killing Carlton Weekly.
claims.quote: After the murder, an informant told Chicago police and FBI agents that a bounty had been offered for killing Weekly: $50,000 at first, later raised to $100,000.

claims.claim: The bounty for killing Carlton Weekly came from O Block rapper King Von.
claims.quote: Prosecutors later alleged the bounty came from O Block rapper King Von.

claims.claim: Ralph Turpin and a friend entered Milani Boutique at approximately 3:59 p.m. and noticed Carlton Weekly.
claims.quote: At approximately 3:59 p.m., Ralph Turpin and a friend of Turpin's entered Milani Boutique and noticed Weekly.

claims.claim: Ralph Turpin made at least one phone call inside Milani Boutique to Carlton Weekly's rival gang members to come downtown to kill Weekly.
claims.quote: Turpin made at least one phone call inside Milani Boutique to Weekly's rival gang members to come downtown to kill Weekly.

claims.claim: Tacarlos Offerd purchased a Ford Fusion used as a lead car in the shooting one week before the August 4, 2020 murder.
claims.quote: Prosecutors said defendant Tacarlos Offerd purchased a vehicle used as a "lead car" in the shooting one week before the August 4, 2020 murder. The vehicle was a Ford Fusion.

claims.claim: The Ford Fusion was returned to a suburban dealership approximately one hour after the shooting.
claims.quote: Julien said the Fusion was returned to the dealership in the Chicago suburbs approximately one hour after the shooting.

claims.claim: The Ford Fusion purchased by Tacarlos Offerd was seen on police POD cameras and license plate readers.
claims.quote: He said the vehicle Offerd purchased was seen on police POD cameras and license plate readers.

claims.claim: Tacarlos Offerd bought a car, but some unknown person was in it and may have driven downtown, with no evidence linking anyone specific to driving it that day.
claims.quote: Offerd's defense attorney, John Somerville, argued there was no evidence linking anyone specific to driving the car that day. "Mr. Offerd bought a car," Somerville said. "Some unknown person was in his car. Some unknown person may have driven downtown."

claims.claim: Tacarlos Offerd drove the Ford Fusion in the shooting with gunmen riding in it.
claims.quote: Prosecutors said Offerd drove the Fusion in the shooting, with gunmen riding in it.

claims.claim: Kenneth Roberson drove the Chrysler 300 in the shooting with gunmen riding in it.
claims.quote: Prosecutors said Kenneth Roberson drove the Chrysler 300, with gunmen riding in it.

claims.claim: Kenneth Roberson called CPD to get his Chrysler 300 back after it was seized.
claims.quote: After the seizure, Roberson called CPD to get it back.

claims.claim: Roberson acknowledged to a cooperating witness as the crew drove toward East Oak Street that he was on his way to murder Carlton Weekly.
claims.quote: As the crew drove toward East Oak Street on August 4, 2020, Roberson made statements to a cooperating witness acknowledging that Roberson was on his way to murder Weekly.

claims.claim: Kenneth Roberson made statements about the murder to a second witness for purposes of concealment.
claims.quote: Roberson later made statements about the murder to a second witness. The filing says those statements were made for purposes of concealment.

claims.claim: The O Block gang publicly claimed responsibility for their violence and used social media and music to increase their criminal enterprise.
claims.quote: The U.S. Attorney's Office said the O Block gang "publicly claimed responsibility for their violence and used social media and music to increase their criminal enterprise."

claims.claim: The defendants believed killing FBG Duck would bring glory to O Block and was about power, status, and retribution.
claims.quote: Prosecutors told the jury the defendants believed killing FBG Duck would bring glory to O Block: it was about power, status, and retribution.

claims.claim: Ralph Turpin placed at least one phone call from inside Milani Boutique reporting Carlton Weekly's location to his rivals.
claims.quote: Ralph Turpin placed at least one phone call from inside Milani Boutique on the afternoon of August 4, 2020. The filing says the call reported Weekly's location to his rivals.

claims.claim: Charles Liggins, Kenneth Roberson, Tacarlos Offerd, Christopher Thomas, Marcus Smart, and Ralph Turpin were members or associates of O Block and murdered Carlton Weekly to maintain and increase their positions in the gang.
claims.quote: The indictment alleged the six were members or associates of the O Block street gang, and that they murdered Carlton Weekly to maintain and increase their positions in the gang.

claims.claim: Ezell Rawls was identified as a fourth gunman in the surveillance video.
claims.quote: News reporting identified a fourth gunman, Ezell Rawls, in the surveillance video.

claims.claim: At trial, Liggins, Thomas, and Smart were gunmen; Roberson drove the Chrysler 300; Offerd drove the Ford Fusion; and Turpin spotted Weekly in the boutique and called it in.
claims.quote: Prosecutors identified the roles at trial: Liggins, Thomas, and Smart were gunmen; Roberson drove the Chrysler 300; Offerd drove the Ford Fusion; Turpin spotted Weekly in the boutique and called it in.

claims.claim: The jury's verdicts hold the six defendants accountable for a murder that took Carlton Weekly's life.
claims.quote: "The jury's verdicts today hold the six defendants accountable for a brutal murder that took the life of Carlton Weekly," Acting U.S. Attorney Morris Pasqual said.

Deputy Chief O'Shea said the shoppers were standing on the sidewalk when a pair of vehicles pulled up, with two gunmen stepping out of each to open fire.
News reporting identified a fourth gunman, Ezell Rawls, in the surveillance video.

machine_events.what: Social media broadcasts by Carlton Weekly of his travels
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020 (that day; no exact timestamps in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves only that police officers at the scene noted Weekly had been broadcasting his travels on social media that day. Does not prove what platform or locations were shown, when posts occurred, or that the attackers used those broadcasts to locate him.
machine_events.quote: Officers noted that Weekly had been broadcasting his travels on social media that day, and that he was found.

machine_events.what: Phone call(s) placed by Ralph Turpin from inside Milani Boutique
machine_events.when_text: Afternoon of August 4, 2020, after approximately 3:59 p.m.
machine_events.proves: Per the federal court filing summary, indicates at least one phone call was placed by Turpin from inside Milani Boutique after ~3:59 p.m. A call record alone can prove a call occurred and its timing, not the spoken contents of the conversation; raw call-detail records and cell-site logs are not in the file.
machine_events.quote: Ralph Turpin placed at least one phone call from inside Milani Boutique on the afternoon of August 4, 2020. The filing says the call reported Weekly's location to his rivals.

machine_events.what: Parkway Gardens apartment complex surveillance video showing four men sprinting down steps into a Ford Fusion and a Chrysler 300
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020, before the shooting (doc04 and doc10 place the crew's departure toward East Oak Street at about 4:02 p.m.; no video timestamp is stated in doc05)
machine_events.proves: Proves four men ran down building steps at Parkway Gardens and got into a waiting Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300. Does not by itself prove the identities of the four men (police released the video asking the public for help identifying them) or who drove either vehicle.
machine_events.quote: Surveillance video from the Parkway Gardens apartments, the South Side complex known as O Block, shows four men sprinting down the steps of a building and getting into two waiting cars: a Ford Fusion and a Chrysler 300.

machine_events.what: Police POD cameras and license plate readers tracking the Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300 from the South Side to the Gold Coast
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020, between departure from Parkway Gardens and the ~4:26 p.m. shooting (no exact camera timestamps in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves the Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300 traveled from the South Side to the Gold Coast. Suggests coordinated movement of both cars, but cannot by itself prove who was driving or riding inside either vehicle.
machine_events.quote: Police POD cameras and license plate readers then tracked the two cars as they drove from the South Side to the Gold Coast.

machine_events.what: Oak Street surveillance video showing the Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300 pulling up and four masked gunmen firing
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020, at the shooting (approximately 4:26 p.m. per doc01, doc04, and doc10; no exact video timestamp stated in doc05)
machine_events.proves: Proves the Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300 arrived on Oak Street and four masked gunmen exited the two vehicles and shot Weekly and two people with him. Because the gunmen were masked, this video alone cannot identify the shooters' faces or the drivers.
machine_events.quote: Video from Oak Street shows the Ford Fusion and the Chrysler 300 pull up. Four gunmen got out of the two cars and shot Weekly and the two people with him. The gunmen at Oak Street were masked.

machine_events.what: Police POD cameras tracking the Ford Fusion and Chrysler 300 back toward Parkway Gardens until they split up
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020, after the ~4:26 p.m. shooting (no exact camera timestamps in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves both vehicles drove back toward Parkway Gardens after the shooting and then separated in different directions. Cannot by itself identify the occupants or document where either car went after splitting up.
machine_events.quote: Police POD cameras tracked the two vehicles as they drove back toward Parkway Gardens after the shooting. The two cars then split up in different directions.

machine_events.what: Purchase of a Ford Fusion by Tacarlos Offerd
machine_events.when_text: One week before the August 4, 2020 murder
machine_events.proves: Based on a prosecutor's detention-hearing statement (and acknowledged as a car purchase by defense counsel in doc06; no underlying bill of sale or receipt is in the file), shows Offerd purchased the Ford Fusion one week before the shooting. Does not by itself prove he drove it on August 4, 2020.
machine_events.quote: Prosecutors said defendant Tacarlos Offerd purchased a vehicle used as a "lead car" in the shooting one week before the August 4, 2020 murder. The vehicle was a Ford Fusion.

machine_events.what: Police POD cameras and license plate readers sighting the Ford Fusion purchased by Tacarlos Offerd
machine_events.when_text: August 4, 2020 (no exact camera timestamps in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves the Ford Fusion Offerd purchased was captured on police POD cameras and license plate readers. Suggests the vehicle's movement in connection with the shooting, but cannot by itself prove Offerd was driving or inside it.
machine_events.quote: He said the vehicle Offerd purchased was seen on police POD cameras and license plate readers.

machine_events.what: Return of the Ford Fusion to a dealership in the Chicago suburbs
machine_events.when_text: Approximately one hour after the August 4, 2020 shooting
machine_events.proves: Based on a prosecutor's detention-hearing statement (no dealership receipt or timestamped return log is included in the file), indicates the Fusion was returned about an hour after the shooting. Does not by itself prove who returned the car or who drove it downtown.
machine_events.quote: Julien said the Fusion was returned to the dealership in the Chicago suburbs approximately one hour after the shooting.

machine_events.what: Phone call from Kenneth Roberson to CPD following seizure of his Chrysler 300
machine_events.when_text: After CPD seized the Chrysler 300 the day after the murder (August 5, 2020 or later; no exact call timestamp in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves Roberson contacted CPD seeking return of the seized Chrysler 300, linking him to an ownership or possession claim over the car. Cannot by itself prove he drove the vehicle during the August 4, 2020 shooting.
machine_events.quote: After the seizure, Roberson called CPD to get it back.

machine_events.what: Defendants' online posts, photos, and videos depicting gang signs, firearms, and the Tookaville feud
machine_events.when_text: Over years (no individual post dates or timestamps in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves defendants created or appeared in public online posts, photos, and videos involving gang signs, firearms, and the Tookaville feud over years. Suggests gang affiliation and rivalry, but does not by itself prove involvement in the August 4, 2020 shooting.
machine_events.quote: Prosecutors built the racketeering case in part from the defendants' own posts, photos, and videos: gang signs, firearms, and the feud with Tookaville carried on in public, in songs and online, over years.

machine_events.what: Video recorded after the murder showing King Von giving defendants diamond O Block pendants and stacks of cash
machine_events.when_text: After the August 4, 2020 murder (no exact recording date or timestamp in file)
machine_events.proves: Proves King Von handed diamond O Block pendants and stacks of cash to defendants on video after the murder. Suggests a post-shooting transfer of valuables and money, but cannot by itself prove the items were payment for a murder bounty.
machine_events.quote: Jurors saw video recorded after the murder in which King Von, the O Block rapper prosecutors said put a price on Weekly's head, gave the defendants diamond O Block pendants and stacks of cash.

record_checks.claim: Prosecutors said Tacarlos Offerd drove the Ford Fusion in the shooting with gunmen riding in it (doc06, doc12).
record_checks.record_says: The machine records cited in doc06 (police POD cameras and license plate readers) and the purchase/return timing establish only the vehicle's purchase, camera sightings, and return. As defense counsel John Somerville argued in doc06, those vehicle records do not by themselves identify who was driving the Ford Fusion that day.
record_checks.quote: Offerd's defense attorney, John Somerville, argued there was no evidence linking anyone specific to driving the car that day. "Mr. Offerd bought a car," Somerville said. "Some unknown person was in his car. Some unknown person may have driven downtown."

record_checks.claim: At the scene on August 4, 2020, police officers noted Weekly had been broadcasting his travels on social media that day and that he was found (doc02).
record_checks.record_says: Later federal court filings summarizing phone and timeline records (doc04, doc10) attribute Weekly's spotting to Ralph Turpin entering Milani Boutique at approximately 3:59 p.m., seeing Weekly inside, and placing at least one phone call from inside the boutique, with the O Block crew moving toward East Oak Street about three minutes later at ~4:02 p.m. The file contains no social media records confirming the attackers located Weekly through his broadcasts.
record_checks.quote: The call came after Turpin entered the boutique at approximately 3:59 p.m. and saw Weekly inside.

record_checks.claim: Federal filings state Ralph Turpin's phone call from inside Milani Boutique reported Weekly's location to his rivals to come downtown to kill him (doc04, doc10).
record_checks.record_says: The summarized timeline shows a call after ~3:59 p.m. followed roughly three minutes later by the O Block crew beginning to move toward East Oak Street at ~4:02 p.m., which aligns with the alleged sequence. However, a phone call record proves only that a call was made and its timing, not the words spoken on the call, and no raw call-detail records or call content appear in the file.
record_checks.quote: At about 4:02 p.m., roughly three minutes after Turpin entered the boutique, the O Block crew began moving toward East Oak Street.

record_checks.claim: Prosecutors said Kenneth Roberson drove the Chrysler 300 in the shooting with gunmen riding in it (doc07, doc12).
record_checks.record_says: The surveillance trail (Parkway Gardens video, Oak Street video, and POD cameras) tracks the Chrysler 300 itself, and Roberson's post-seizure call to CPD links him to wanting the car back (doc07), but the machine records described in the file do not by themselves identify the driver; prosecutors also cited cooperating witness statements in doc08.
record_checks.quote: The Chrysler appears with the Ford Fusion in the surveillance trail: out of Parkway Gardens before the shooting, on Oak Street at the shooting, and tracked back toward the South Side after it.

record_checks.claim: Prosecutors identified Liggins, Thomas, and Smart as gunmen (doc12), and news reporting identified Ezell Rawls as a fourth gunman in the surveillance video (doc11).
record_checks.record_says: Doc05 states the gunmen captured on Oak Street surveillance video were masked, so the Oak Street footage alone cannot identify their faces; police also released the Parkway Gardens video seeking public help to identify the four men entering the cars (doc05), and doc11 does not specify which surveillance video was used to identify Rawls.
record_checks.quote: The gunmen at Oak Street were masked.

record_checks.claim: An informant reported a $50,000 bounty (later raised to $100,000) for killing Weekly, which prosecutors alleged came from King Von (doc03).
record_checks.record_says: Post-murder video shown at trial depicts King Von giving defendants diamond O Block pendants and stacks of cash (doc09). While consistent with a post-shooting distribution of cash and jewelry, the video alone does not prove a prior $50,000-$100,000 bounty agreement, and doc03 notes the bounty was an allegation and King Von was never charged.
record_checks.quote: Jurors saw video recorded after the murder in which King Von, the O Block rapper prosecutors said put a price on Weekly's head, gave the defendants diamond O Block pendants and stacks of cash.

lead_detective.brief:
THE CASE IN FIVE LINES
On August 4, 2020, at approximately 3:59 p.m., Ralph Turpin entered Milani Boutique on East Oak Street, saw rapper Carlton Weekly shopping, and placed at least one phone call reporting Weekly's location (doc04, doc10). By ~4:02 p.m., men from Parkway Gardens (O Block) departed in two cars—a Ford Fusion and a Chrysler 300—tracked by surveillance, Police POD cameras, and license plate readers to the Gold Coast (doc04, doc05). At ~4:26 p.m. near the 100 block of East Oak Street, four masked gunmen exited the two vehicles and shot Weekly multiple times while wounding two others; Weekly was pronounced dead at Northwestern Memorial Hospital about half an hour later (~4:56 p.m.) (doc01, doc05). Police recovered one weapon at the scene (doc02), the Ford Fusion was returned to a suburban dealership about an hour after the shooting (doc06), and CPD seized Kenneth Roberson's Chrysler 300 the next day (doc07). Six men (Liggins, Roberson, Offerd, Thomas, Smart, and Turpin) were federally indicted and convicted on January 17, 2024, though the case file here consists of news and court summaries without an evidence ledger or medical examiner report (doc11, doc12).

THE STRONGEST CONTRADICTION
Severity: High (doc06 vs. doc06 — Identity of the Ford Fusion driver during the shooting)
- Quote A (doc06): "Offerd's defense attorney, John Somerville, argued there was no evidence linking anyone specific to driving the car that day. 'Mr. Offerd bought a car,' Somerville said. 'Some unknown person was in his car. Some unknown person may have driven downtown.'"
- Quote B (doc06): "Prosecutors said Offerd drove the Fusion in the shooting, with gunmen riding in it."
- File Note: These conflicting statements arise from adversarial arguments at Offerd's October 15, 2021 federal detention hearing; the file lacks the underlying camera images, dealership return records, or forensic logs identifying who drove or returned the Fusion.

THE ALIBI TABLE
- Tacarlos Offerd | Window: 2020-08-04 ~16:26 to ~16:56 | Rating: Contradicted | Basis: Defense counsel stated at the detention hearing that "Some unknown person was in his car. Some unknown person may have driven downtown" (doc06), whereas prosecutors stated "Offerd drove the Fusion in the shooting, with gunmen riding in it" (doc06).

THE TOP THREE LEADS
1. [Score: 100 | 40+25+20+15] Pull the authenticated East Oak Street surveillance footage, Police POD camera footage, and LPR hit sheets from ~16:26 on August 4, 2020 (doc05, doc06) to determine whether the driver of the Ford Fusion is visible or identifiable during the shooting.
2. [Score: 80 | 40+25+15] Have the detective interview Tacarlos Offerd (or review his subpoenaed cell-site records) and ask the exact question: who had possession of the Ford Fusion between 15:59 and 17:26 on August 4, 2020, and who returned it to the suburban dealership (doc06)?
3. [Score: 75 | 40+20+15] Pull the suburban dealership return records, dealership surveillance footage, and any CPD/FBI forensic inspection logs for the Ford Fusion returned ~17:26 on August 4, 2020 (doc06) to prove or disprove who returned the vehicle.

THE GAP LIST
- Master evidence ledger: Missing entirely from the file (proven by doc01, doc02, doc05, doc06, doc07, doc09, doc10).
- Autopsy & medical examiner report: No official cause/manner of death report for Carlton Weekly (proven by doc01).
- Scene weapon & ballistics ledger: No property entry or ballistics report for the 1 weapon recovered at the scene vs. 4 shooters (proven by doc01, doc02).
- Chrysler 300 seizure & forensic logs: Seized by CPD on 2020-08-05 but no impound or forensic reports in file (proven by doc07).
- Ford Fusion dealership & inspection records: Purchased 1 week prior and returned ~1 hour after shooting, but no records in file (proven by doc06).
- Surveillance & LPR exhibits: No video files or logs for Parkway Gardens, East Oak Street, POD cameras, or LPRs (proven by doc05, doc06).
- Ralph Turpin phone records: Call from Milani Boutique summarized in filing, but no CDRs in file (proven by doc04, doc10).
- Weekly's August 4, 2020 social media broadcast: Noted by officers at scene, no preserved record in file (proven by doc02).
- Post-shooting pendant/cash video & financial records: Shown to jurors at trial, absent from file ledger (proven by doc09).
- Songs & social media exhibits: "Dead Bitches" release and defendants' posts referenced, absent from file ledger (proven by doc03, doc09).
